info.title: BrowserGlass Gateway REST API
info.description: The REST surface of a BrowserGlass gateway (@browserglass/server), hand-written alongside packages/server/src/rest/router.ts's route table so the two do not drift silently (see packages/server/test/rest/openapi-drift.test.ts). HTTP is request/response: a caller wanting a live feed (frames, console, network) still needs the WebSocket transport (bgls.v1) or a poll loop against these routes, never a push from here. Routes tagged 'stub' are registered but answer 501 Not Implemented; every other route is live.

servers.description: Default mount point; see createBrowserGlass()'s mountPath option.

post.summary: Acquire (launch or reuse) a browser instance

schema.description: AcquireRequest: spec, sticky affinity, subject, metadata, etc.

get.summary: The open instances a caller may see, with live titles/URLs and a count
get.description: The confirm-before-destroy surface: enough identity (createdBy, metadata, lifetime, live target titles/URLs) to tell two same-spec browsers apart before ending one, plus totalCount so "how many are open" needs no client-side arithmetic across pages. Every InstanceLifecycleState except released/failed is 'open'; state, when given, must be one of the open ones (released/failed are refused with a pointer to GET /v1/instances/{instanceId}/history instead). targetsLive/targetsObservedAt make staleness explicit: targets are read from a live ManagedSession already attached in this gateway process (free, no new CDP connection triggered), never guessed or fetched by attaching on demand. See packages/server/src/rest/routes/inventory.ts's own module doc for the live-versus-cached argument and the redaction/cross-node-honesty precedent this follows.

200.description: A page of open instances, plus the unpaged total

patch.description: Registered but not wired: this build answers 501 with a stub error body naming the route. See packages/server/src/rest/router.ts's STUB_PATHS table.

post.summary: Attach to (or re-affirm) an instance as a viewer

get.summary: What happened to this browser, readable after it is gone
get.description: Reads the instances store row directly (not through BrowserRouter.describe(), which answers E_INSTANCE_GONE for exactly the released row this route exists to still answer for), and folds in whatever audit_events rows exist for this instanceId (Store.queryAudit; empty until a concurrent change makes audit writing real, at which point this route's auditEvents starts carrying rows with no further change here). firstViewerAt/releaseReason/restartCount/peakRssMib/osPid are named in historyFieldsUnavailable and reported null: those five live only on the raw instances table row and are not yet carried onto the Instance domain entity Store.getInstance returns; closing that gap needs a new Store method, out of this route's ownership. When the instances row itself has left its retention window but audit rows for it survive (audit_events carries no foreign key to instances by design), instanceRecordFound is false and the response is built from the audit trail alone rather than 404ing outright. See packages/server/src/rest/routes/inventory.ts's own module doc.

200.description: This instance's lifecycle history, and its audit trail if any

delete.description: Registered but not wired: this build answers 501 with a stub error body naming the route. See packages/server/src/rest/router.ts's STUB_PATHS table.

get.summary: List viewers currently attached to a session
List targets (tabs) open in an instance
get.description: A poll, not a feed: use the WebSocket transport's target.list/target.updated for live updates.

post.summary: Navigate a target: goto, back, forward, reload, or stop
post.description: Answers once the navigation command is acknowledged, not once the page finishes loading; poll GET .../targets or use the WebSocket transport's nav.state for load completion.

200.description: Navigation state, or {navigated:true} when the driver has none to report

get.summary: Capture one screenshot of a target
get.description: One image, not a stream: for a live feed, subscribe to the target's stream over the WebSocket transport instead.

post.summary: Dispatch a click or a type into a target
post.description: Requires the caller to hold (borrows and releases per call) the target's control lease, the same as a WebSocket caller.

post.summary: Raw CDP passthrough, one allowlisted method at a time
post.description: Off by default, granted by no role bundle: a token must name the cdp capability explicitly. The method must be on cdp-passthrough-allowlist.ts's allowlist, checked before a live sender is even looked for, so a disallowed method is refused the same way whether or not this build has one wired.

put.summary: Append a chunk of raw bytes to a staged upload
put.description: Body is raw bytes, not JSON, appended at the current offset. Resume by re-reading GET /v1/upload/:uploadId for the received offset.

get.summary: Get an upload's resume point and status

post.summary: Attach staged uploads to a file input
post.description: Names uploadIds, never a filesystem path: see files/safe-name.ts for why no route here accepts a caller-supplied path.

get.summary: Fetch a completed download by its one-shot signed token
get.description: Public: no bearer token, no Principal resolved at all. The signed URL token itself is the authorization. Consumed exactly once; a second fetch of the same token 404s.
Registered but not wired: this build answers 501 with a stub error body naming the route. See packages/server/src/rest/router.ts's STUB_PATHS table.

get.summary: Who is viewing and who is controlling this instance right now
get.description: Live presence, out of band from the bgls.v1 WebSocket: per-viewer controlling/watching/idle state, a viewer/controlling count, and which targets have more than one simultaneous controller (contendedTargets). Answers correctly only for an instance whose live session is on THIS gateway process (live:false with an empty roster otherwise, never a guessed answer); see packages/server/src/rest/routes/presence.ts's own module doc for the cross-node caveat and the known kind/joinedAt gap (presenceFieldsUnavailable).

delete.summary: Forcibly disconnect one viewer from a session
delete.description: The operator's tool for correcting a misbehaving connected viewer (human, agent, or CDP client): sends a goodbye envelope naming the reason, then closes that viewer's socket. Leaves every other viewer on the session untouched.

bearerAuth.description: An EdDSA-signed, capability-scoped token issued by POST /v1/tokens (or an app credential). GET /v1/downloads/:token is the one route that needs none.

ErrorBody.description: The one error envelope shape every REST response uses.

Error.description: An error, in the standard envelope
